corpus_definition: A shape that looks like part of a circle.

forms.definition: a curved shape that is part of a circle
forms.example: The bird flew in a graceful arc over the lake.

syn.note: Easy, general word for any bent line; an arc is a curve like part of a circle.
Exactly half of a circle; an arc can be any part of a circle.
A place where a road or river changes direction; not always round.

forms.definition: to move through the air in a curved line
forms.example: The ball arced over the goalkeeper and into the net.

syn.note: Very close: to move in a bent line.
To move from side to side or in a curve, like a door or a bat.

forms.note: There is no common adjective made from arc. Use curved.
There is no adverb made from arc.

context.text: In the football match in Tashkent, the ball arced high over the players. Everyone watched its long arc before it landed in the net.

reviewer_note: Kept the shape sense; arc (verb) is a conversion. The electric-arc meaning and the word arch are left out.

corpus_definition: Relating to the art of designing buildings and large structures.

forms.definition: the art and style of designing buildings
forms.example: Samarkand is famous for its beautiful old architecture.

syn.note: Design is the plan for how anything looks or works, not only buildings.
Construction is the work of building, not the art of planning it.

forms.note: There is no common verb in this family. Use design.

forms.definition: connected with the design of buildings
forms.example: The bridge has a very unusual architectural style.

syn.note: About how something is built and holds together, not about its style.

forms.definition: in a way connected with the design of buildings
forms.example: The old city of Khiva is architecturally very interesting.

syn.note: About how something is built, not about its style or beauty.

people.definition: a person whose job is to design buildings
people.example: The architect showed us the plans for the new school.

context.text: Many tourists come to Samarkand to see its architecture. The Registan has great architectural beauty, and the whole square is architecturally unique.

reviewer_note: Verb slot no_form: 'architect' as a verb is only computing jargon, not in learner dictionaries.

forms.definition: a pleasant smell, especially of food or drink
forms.example: The aroma of fresh coffee filled the whole kitchen.

syn.note: Easy, general word; a smell can be good or bad.
A pleasant smell, often of flowers or perfume.
A sweet, pleasant smell; often used for perfume.

ant.note: A very unpleasant smell; a bit formal.

forms.note: There is no verb made from aroma.

forms.definition: having a strong and pleasant smell
forms.example: My grandmother adds aromatic herbs like dill to her soup.

syn.note: Very close; often used for flowers and perfume.
Easy, clear way to say the same thing.

forms.note: There is no common adverb made from aroma.

context.text: The aroma of fresh bread came from the bakery near the bazaar. Inside, my aunt was buying aromatic spices for her plov.

reviewer_note: No affix claimed on aromatic: removing -ic leaves no real word. Aromatherapy is a compound and is left out.

corpus_definition: A belief that something is true without needing proof.

forms.definition: a belief that something is true without any proof
forms.example: His assumption about the test was completely wrong.

syn.note: Easy word; a guess is an idea you are not sure about.
Very close but formal and less common.
Close; often used in law and formal writing.
Something you think is true; it can have strong reasons behind it.

ant.note: A fact is shown to be true; this is only believed.

forms.definition: to think something is true without being sure
forms.example: I assumed you were busy, so I didn't call.

syn.note: Very close and common in speaking.
Close but a little more formal.
Easy, general word; you may have proof or not.
To think something will happen in the future.

forms.definition: used about a name that is false, not your real one
forms.example: The thief stayed at the hotel under an assumed name.
forms.note: Belongs to assume = take on or pretend, not believing something without proof.
There is no common adverb in this family.

context.text: I made the assumption that the bus would come on time. I assumed wrong, and I was late for my first class.

reviewer_note: No affix claimed: removing -tion from assumption leaves no real word. assumed (adj) kept as other_meaning (false name).

corpus_definition: A large rock that moves through space around the sun.

forms.definition: a large rock that moves around the sun in space
forms.example: The asteroid passed close to the Earth last night.

syn.note: A small space rock that burns and shines as it falls through the air.
A piece of space rock that has landed on the Earth.
A ball of ice and dust in space with a long bright tail.

forms.note: There is no verb made from asteroid.
There is no common adjective; asteroidal is only used by scientists.
There is no adverb made from asteroid.

context.text: Scientists in many countries watched a small asteroid last week. They said the asteroid was about the size of a bus and was no danger to us.

reviewer_note: Single-form family; -oid is not in the affix table, so no affix is claimed.

forms.definition: the act of listening, watching or thinking carefully about something
forms.example: Please pay attention to the teacher.

syn.note: Close: keeping your mind on one thing.
Close and a little informal.
Used in 'take notice of': seeing something, not always for long.

ant.note: Not listening or watching carefully; formal.
Something that takes your mind away from what you are doing.

forms.definition: the quality of listening and watching carefully
forms.example: The nurse was known for her attentiveness to every patient.

forms.definition: being present at school, work or an event
forms.example: Attendance at the meeting was very low.
forms.note: Belongs to attend = go to or be present, not listening carefully.

forms.definition: to listen to or deal with something carefully
forms.example: Please attend to what I am saying.
forms.note: In this meaning it is used with 'to'. The more common meaning is 'go to' (attend school).

syn.note: Everyday phrase with the same meaning.
Easy word: use your ears carefully.
To keep your mind on one thing.

ant.note: To give no attention to someone or something.

forms.definition: listening and watching carefully
forms.example: The teacher was happy with her attentive students.

syn.note: Quick to notice things; ready.
Watching carefully, often for danger.
Keeping your mind on one thing.
Easy word: thinking about what you do to avoid mistakes.

forms.definition: in a way that shows you are listening and watching carefully
forms.example: The children listened attentively to the story.

syn.note: Easy word with a similar meaning.
Used with watch or listen: 'listen closely'.
With great interest and full attention.

people.definition: a person whose job is to help or serve people
people.example: The flight attendant brought us some water.
people.note: Belongs to attend = look after or serve people, not listening carefully.

people.definition: a person who goes to a meeting or event
people.example: Every attendee got a free bag at the conference.
people.note: Belongs to attend = go to an event.

context.text: The students were very attentive during the lesson. They listened attentively and gave the teacher their full attention.

reviewer_note: attend kept as existing only in the formal 'attend to' sense; attendance, attendant and attendee are other_meaning (go to / serve). Opposites inattentive and inattention are in ant lists.

forms.definition: how easy it is to hear a sound
forms.example: The new microphones improved the audibility of the speakers.

syn.note: How clear a sound or picture is.

forms.note: There is no verb made from audible. Audition comes from the same old Latin root (hear) but is not made from audible.

forms.definition: loud enough for people to hear
forms.example: Her soft voice was barely audible in the big room.

syn.note: Easy to hear or understand.
Easy to hear and separate from other sounds.
Formal: able to be noticed with any sense, not only hearing.

forms.definition: in a way that people can hear
forms.example: The whole class sighed audibly when the teacher gave homework.

syn.note: In a voice that others can hear.
Easy, everyday phrase with the same meaning.
In a way that is easy to hear or understand.

context.text: The teacher's voice was hardly audible at the back of the hall. When the microphone started working, everyone sighed audibly with relief.

reviewer_note: audience, auditorium and audition share the Latin root but are not made from audible, so they are not forms or people.

corpus_definition: Showing that you are in charge and know things.

forms.definition: the power to give orders and make people obey
forms.example: The head teacher has the authority to change the rules.

syn.note: Easy, general word; power can be official or not.
The ability to make people or things do what you want.
Control over a group, often in the army.

forms.definition: to give official permission for something
forms.example: The manager authorized the payment.
forms.note: Belongs to authority = official right to allow things, not a confident manner. British spelling: authorise.

forms.definition: showing that you are in charge and know a lot
forms.example: She spoke in an authoritative tone of voice.

syn.note: Showing power and making people want to obey.
Easy word: sure of yourself, but not always in charge.
Saying clearly what you want or think.
Strong and not easy to change.

forms.definition: making people obey strict rules and not giving them freedom
forms.example: The country had an authoritarian government for many years.
forms.note: Belongs to authority = strict control over people; it is negative, while this word is usually positive.

forms.definition: in a confident way that shows you are in charge
forms.example: The captain spoke authoritatively to the team.

syn.note: In a way that shows you are sure of yourself.
In a strong way that does not change.

context.text: Our new manager speaks in an authoritative voice, so everyone listens. She has the authority to change the rules, and she explains them authoritatively.

reviewer_note: Anchored to the confident/in-charge sense; the 'reliable source' sense (an authoritative book) is not used. authorize and authoritarian are other_meaning; author is not made from this family.

corpus_definition: The name of a famous person written by them.

forms.definition: a famous person's name, written by them for a fan
forms.example: Can I have your autograph, please?

syn.note: Anyone's name written by them, for example on a document; this word is for famous people and fans.

forms.definition: to write your name on something for a fan
forms.example: The singer autographed hundreds of photos after the concert.

syn.note: Easy, general word for writing your name.

forms.definition: signed by a famous person
forms.example: He has an autographed football from the national team.

syn.note: Same meaning and very common: 'a signed photo'.

forms.note: There is no adverb made from autograph.

context.text: At the concert in Tashkent, my sister asked the singer for his autograph. He autographed her ticket, and now the autographed ticket hangs on her wall.

reviewer_note: auto- and -graph are not in the affix table, so no affix is claimed.

corpus_definition: To be of help or use in achieving something.

forms.definition: use or help in getting a result
forms.example: We tried to call him, but to no avail.
forms.note: Almost always in the phrases 'to no avail' and 'of no avail'.

syn.note: Easy word: 'of no use' means the same as 'of no avail'.
'To no avail' means 'without success'.
Easy, general word for making something easier.

forms.definition: to help someone or be useful in getting a result
forms.example: Nothing we tried availed us in the end.
forms.note: Old-fashioned. Also formal 'avail yourself of something' = use it.

syn.note: Easy, everyday word with a similar meaning.
To be good or useful for someone.
Formal word for help.

ant.note: To make it harder for someone to do something.

forms.definition: able to be used, bought or found
forms.example: Tickets are available at the station.
forms.note: Belongs to avail = something you can use or get, not being of help in getting a result.
There is no adverb in this family.

context.text: We looked for my lost phone all evening, but to no avail. In the end, nothing we did availed us until a taxi driver brought it back.

reviewer_note: CORPUS: definition is a verb but the example uses the noun ('of no avail'); map anchored to the verb, noun included as conversion. available kept as other_meaning.
